proposed.sourceName: Darul Ifta Birmingham — 'Ruling of Carmine (E120) Cochineal Insects' (Maulana Mohammed Haroon Hussain)
proposed.paraphrase: This Hanafi fatwa rules carmine (E120), derived from cochineal insects, impermissible to consume: insects fall under khabaith (things sound human disposition finds repugnant), and only locusts, extreme necessity, or negligible unavoidable amounts are excepted — carmine is added deliberately and avoidably, so it does not qualify.

proposed.sourceName: Darul-Ifta, al-Jamia al-Ulum al-Islamiyya (Binnori Town) — 'Ruling on Carmine in Food' via SeekersGuidance (Mawlana Ilyas Patel)
proposed.paraphrase: Per the majority of jurists, consuming carmine (cochineal insect dye) in food is impermissible because insects are khabaith (vile things) per Qur'an 7:157; the pigment is ritually pure for wudu and permissible in cosmetics, but not lawful to eat.

researcherNote: E120 seeded general = grade 4 (Questionable — widely avoided). Carmine is unambiguously insect-derived (single-possibility E-number); the majority position (Hanafi/Shafi'i/Hanbali) treats insects other than locust as khabaith, so mainstream/general practice avoids it. Two independent tier-1 Hanafi darul-ifta fatwas, both directly ruling impermissible. High-traffic -> two independent sources. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
